tasks.short: Confer with clients on objectives and approaches

steps.what: State objectives, budget and background information
Draft presentation approaches from that information

loop.output: approach notes each citing one objective id
loop.check: Every approach cites an objective id from the form
loop.stop: One pass; drop any sentence with no objective id
loop.why_not_simpler: How to open a presentation is not a fixed mail merge

steps.what: Confer with clients on styles and techniques
Determine the approaches this brief will use
File the client brief after that determination

tasks.design: The client states objectives, budget and background on a {PROJECT} form sent by {EMAIL}. A bounded note in {DOCS} drafts presentation approaches from those fields only. The art director confers with the client, chooses styles and techniques, and files the brief in {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Background arrived as conversation notes, so a brief could not show which objective it came from.
tasks.enabler_now: Objectives, budget and background can be fields with one client id before the meeting.
tasks.still_hard: Hearing what the client actually wants still happens in the room.
tasks.human_edge: The art director determines which approaches, styles and techniques this brief will use.
tasks.altitude: The brief is no longer rebuilt from memory. The conference with the client stays, and the art director can leave an approach blank when no objective supports it.

reach.task: Start a design session from this client brief
reach.learn: Which objectives and budget limits the client stated

evidence.claim: A client briefing is a conversation. The notes can be structured. The choice of approach cannot be taken from the form.

assumptions: Focal role is the art director. The task ends at the filed brief. Designing the layout is a later task.

Input contract: client id, objective, budget amount, background note, presentation date. Producer is the client. If the form is empty the art director types the same fields after the meeting and marks them manual.
Use the document template for the brief before custom code. The meeting prior matches this task and is not treated as desk work.
unknowns: Whether the client will fill a form before the meeting.
Who may choose an approach when the art director is away.
research_questions: How often does the brief lack a budget figure?
How often does the meeting change the written objectives?

already_counted.description: Time in the client conference stays with the art director
Choosing approaches at the end of the briefing stays

incremental.description: Revise the brief template when a new objective type appears
Clients correct an objective the form could not store

approvals.approved_version: approaches chosen for this client brief

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes clients still will not use the form, so the art director writes the brief from notes. The high case assumes a clean form but the conference and the choice of approach still happen in full. Layout production is not counted as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Specify the layout design and material details

steps.what: Read the brief for photographs, graphics and animation
Draft a basic layout design as a starting frame

loop.input: brief fields and the layout template
loop.output: a frame labelled draft with a field citation on each block
loop.check: Each block cites a brief field, and the frame is marked draft
loop.stop: One pass; stop a block that has no field
loop.why_not_simpler: A fixed template cannot judge whether the layout is the right one

steps.what: Specify material details, style, video and sound
Approve the layout design and any required marks
File the approved design with credential metadata

tasks.design: A bounded draft in {DOCS} proposes a basic layout from the brief fields, and that frame is labelled draft. The art director specifies material details such as style, photographs, graphics, animation, video and sound. The art director approves the layout design, including any required synthetic-media mark, and only then is it filed in {CMS} with content-credential metadata.
tasks.previous_blocker: Material details lived in the picture itself, so a later check could not tell type size from a guess.
tasks.enabler_now: Style, photograph count, graphic id and video length can be fields next to the frame.
tasks.still_hard: Whether the layout is the right one is still the art director's judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The art director approves the layout design. A generated frame is not that approval.

ambition.what: Sign the layout spec when material details change, not only at the final proof

tasks.altitude: The blank page takes less time. Specifying and signing stay. The art director can stop a file whose material fields do not match the frame.

reach.task: Build from the signed material details
reach.learn: Which type, photographs and graphics are specified and which are still open

evidence.claim: Specifying a layout is document and screen work. A meeting may review it later. The prior that puts most of this task in meetings overstates the conference and understates the spec.

Digest [S2] and [S3] describe a design tool that drafts from a prompt and a campaign-layout tool that fills locked areas. A person still approves the layout. A generated frame is not the approved design.
Digest [S1] says content-credential metadata can be attached to a creative file. That is metadata, not a judgement that the layout is good.
Digest [S9] and [S10] describe EU transparency duties for synthetic media. A published image or video that a model made is marked before it goes out, and a person confirms the mark.
Digest [S11] reports that campaign images often omit that mark. The mark check is mandatory before this spec is treated as ready to share.
Digest [S12], [S13] and [S14] say copyright in a model-made image is unsettled. The art director does not treat a generated image as owned.
Digest [S7] says a vendor reports that large firms use its design products. The report gives no measured saving, and none is counted here.

assumptions: Focal role is the art director. The task ends at the signed spec. Client presentation and proofing are later tasks.

Input contract: brief id, page size, style, photograph ids, graphic ids, animation flag, video length, sound note. Producer is the art director from the client brief. Missing ids stay blank and are not invented.
Test the document template and its required fields before custom code. This is a page layout, not a spatial room plan, so a space-planning modeller is not used.
unknowns: Which briefs already name photograph and graphic ids.
Whether video in the spec is model-made or shot.
research_questions: How often does a signed spec lack a type style?
How often is a generated frame later mistaken for the approved layout?

already_counted.description: Art director reworks the draft frame before specifying
Specifying material details stays with the art director

incremental.description: Update layout fields when a new media type is added

approvals.approved_version: layout design signed with material details and marks

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes briefs are still prose, so the art director specifies every detail by hand and the draft rarely fires. The high case assumes fields are present but every layout is still signed by the art director. A vendor claim of wide product use is not counted as a saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Review and approve proofs of printed copy

steps.what: Submit art materials and proofs of printed copy
Check proofs against the written print rules
Review art materials and copy materials
Approve proofs of printed copy once marks are confirmed
Send the approved proofs to the production head

tasks.design: Staff submit proofs and materials on a {PROJECT} item. A checker compares the file with the written print rules and only lists mismatches. The art director reviews the materials and approves the proofs, and stops if a model-made image has no confirmed mark. Only that signed version is sent onward by {EMAIL} and stored in {CMS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Proof comments and print defects were mixed in mail, so a pass could not tell a rule miss from a design objection.
tasks.enabler_now: Print rules can be a profile the file is compared with, separate from the art director's approval.
tasks.still_hard: Whether the proof is good enough to print is still a judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The art director approves the proofs. The rule report does not decide the design.

ambition.what: Sign each proof round when it arrives, instead of batching rounds at the end of the week

tasks.altitude: Rule mismatches are listed before the review. The sign-off stays. The art director can refuse to send a proof that has no signature.

reach.task: Release only the proof version the art director signed
reach.learn: Which mismatches were left open and which proof version was approved

evidence.claim: Proof review is a decision on materials someone else prepared. Comparing a file with print rules is the mechanical part.
Digest [S5] says a prepress checker compares a file to print rules and reports each mismatch. It does not decide the design.
Digest [S9] and [S10] describe EU transparency duties for synthetic media. A published image that a model made is marked before it goes out, and a person confirms the mark.
Digest [S11] reports that campaign images often omit that mark. The mark check is mandatory in this design.

assumptions: Focal role is the art director. The task ends when the signed proof is sent. Negotiating with the printer is a different task.

Input contract: proof id, spec id, staff id, page count, model-made yes or no, mark status. Producer is the staff designer. A proof with no spec id is not checked and waits for the art director to link it by hand.
Use the print profile already in the file tool before custom code. The checker never approves a proof.
unknowns: Which print rules this firm actually requires.
Whether copy approval sits with the art director or with the copy desk.
research_questions: What share of proofs fail a print-rule check before anyone reads them?
How often is a proof sent without a recorded approval?

already_counted.description: Art director still reads the materials before signing
Proof sign-off stays with the art director

incremental.description: Update the print-rule profile when a new press profile is adopted
Staff resubmit proofs the profile could not open

approvals.approved_version: proof of printed copy signed in this review

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes proof files are unstructured, so the rule check rarely runs and the art director still hunts defects by hand. The high case assumes clean files but every proof is still signed by the art director. Printing the job is not counted as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Create custom illustrations and graphic elements

steps.what: Read the request for custom illustrations
Agree which graphic elements the piece needs
Propose graphic elements from the written request

loop.input: element list and the request fields
loop.check: Each element cites a request field and is labelled proposal
loop.stop: One pass; return nothing if the subject field is blank
loop.why_not_simpler: A template cannot draw a custom piece

steps.what: Create the custom illustrations at the screen
Accept custom illustrations and clear rights and marks
File the illustration version cleared for use

tasks.design: A short direction review agrees the graphic elements. A bounded pass in {CMS} may propose starting elements from the {DOCS} brief, and those proposals are not the illustration. The art director creates the custom illustrations, then accepts them only after rights are cleared and any model-made image is marked. That version is filed in {CMS} with content-credential metadata.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requests were a sentence in mail, so a starting proposal had nothing structured to cite.
tasks.enabler_now: The request can name subject, count and use before anyone draws.
tasks.still_hard: The illustration itself is still made by the art director.
tasks.human_edge: The art director creates the illustration and does not treat a generated image as owned or as finished.
tasks.altitude: The blank start is shorter. Drawing, rights and the mark stay. The art director can refuse to file an illustration that has no release decision.

reach.task: Place only the illustration version that was cleared
reach.learn: Which elements were accepted and whether rights and marks are done

evidence.claim: Custom illustration is making. A proposal can start the page. It does not finish the piece. The meeting prior on this task is mostly overstated: the work is at the screen, with a short direction review.
Digest [S8] is a commentary that generative tools change craft and that a person still directs the work. It is not a measured saving.
Digest [S2] and [S3] describe design-tool generation and a campaign-layout product. A person still approves the layout. A generated frame is not the approved design.
Digest [S1] says content-credential metadata can be attached to a creative file. That is metadata, not a judgement that the illustration is good.
Digest [S12], [S13] and [S14] say copyright in a model-made image is unsettled. The art director does not treat a generated image as owned, and a person clears rights before external use.
Digest [S9] and [S10] describe EU transparency duties for synthetic media. A person confirms the mark before a model-made image goes out.
Digest [S11] reports that campaign images often omit that mark. The mark check is mandatory in this design.

assumptions: Focal role is the art director. The task ends when the cleared illustration is filed. Placing it in a layout is a later task.

Input contract: request id, subject, element count, use, model-made yes or no. Producer is the requester. If subject or use is blank the art director does not start a proposal and writes the brief by hand.
Use the asset store's version fields before custom code. No generated image is treated as owned.
unknowns: What share of requests are for a model-made start versus a drawn piece.
Who the rights holder is when the client supplied a reference.
research_questions: How often is a proposal used only as a start?
How often does rights clearance block a file?

already_counted.description: Drawing time on the custom illustration stays
Rights and mark clearance stays with the art director

incremental.description: Keep request fields and mark labels aligned with new illustration types

approvals.approved_version: illustration accepted with rights cleared and marks confirmed

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes requests stay vague, so no proposal is drafted and the art director draws from a blank page. The high case assumes a usable start but the drawing, the rights check and the mark still take their time. A vendor use claim is not counted as a saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The week keeps the client briefing, the layout judgement, the proof sign-off and the drawing, and spends less time on a blank page or a manual rule check.
reach: Staff designers receive a signed layout spec with material details, not a raw generated frame.
The production head receives proofs only after the art director has signed that version.
Creative directors can read the client brief that names the approaches discussed.
skills_to_grow: Specify type, photographs and graphics as fields, not only as a picture.
Treat a generated frame as a draft until the layout is signed.
Read a print-rule report without letting it decide the proof.
role.ambitious_version: Every layout spec names its material details, and no proof is sent until the art director has signed that version.
